knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian Determinant of a Transformation

question.:question/problem: Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T\left(\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\right)=\begin{bmatrix}e^{5 u + 5 v} \\ \ln{\left(u v \right)}\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=e^{5 u + 5 v}$ and $y(u,v)=\ln{\left(u v \right)}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=5 e^{5 u + 5 v}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=5 e^{5 u + 5 v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=\frac{1}{u}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=\frac{1}{v}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}5 e^{5 u + 5 v}&5 e^{5 u + 5 v}\\\frac{1}{u}&\frac{1}{v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(5 e^{5 u + 5 v}\right)\cdot\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(5 e^{5 u + 5 v}\right)\cdot\left(\frac{1}{u}\right)\\&=\frac{5 e^{5 u + 5 v}}{v}-\frac{5 e^{5 u + 5 v}}{u}\\&=\frac{\left(5 u - 5 v\right) e^{5 u + 5 v}}{u v}.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \frac{\left(5 u - 5 v\right) e^{5 u + 5 v}}{u v}

question.:question/problem: Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T\left(\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\right)=\begin{bmatrix}u \ln{\left(v \right)} \\ 5 u^{2} v^{2}\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x=u \ln{\left(v \right)}$ and $y=5 u^{2} v^{2}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=\ln{\left(v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=\frac{u}{v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=10 u v^{2}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=10 u^{2} v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}\ln{\left(v \right)}&\frac{u}{v}\\10 u v^{2}&10 u^{2} v\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(\ln{\left(v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(10 u^{2} v\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)\cdot\left(10 u v^{2}\right)\\&=10 u^{2} v \left(\ln{\left(v \right)} - 1\right).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T\left(\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\right)=\begin{bmatrix}\cos{\left(u + v \right)} \\ 2 u + 4 v\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x=\cos{\left(u + v \right)}$ and $y=2 u + 4 v.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=2&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}&- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\\2&4\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(4\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(2\right)\\&=- 2 \sin{\left(u + v \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$
